title: Composition, Transactions and Cross-Operation Atomicity
results: Composition, sequence, Compound Operation and Transaction are distinct.
A Transaction requires a named owner/domain and commit/abort contract over a declared participant state/effect set.
Atomicity is owner-scoped all-or-none commit and is distinct from durability, isolation, consistency and semantic success.
Current admission is a true Registry-local SQLite transaction binding Job, Attempt, reservation, idempotency and relevant Runtime-owned side truth.
Admission commit precedes physical dispatch; a committed Accepted Job before launch is a valid durable-handoff state rather than transaction corruption.
Admission to dispatch is durable handoff and dispatch_issued is an at-most-once handoff fence, not a SQLite-plus-systemd distributed transaction.
One process execution is not one transactional Effect because target code may commit many independent external effects.
Current workspace.execPlan is ordered orchestration rather than transactionality; stop-on-error does not rollback prior step effects.
Partial commit across open-world effects must remain explicit when no shared commit protocol exists.
Distributed transactions require actual participant prepare/commit/abort/recovery semantics; preflight checks are not prepare votes.
2PC shows atomic safety can block under coordinator failure while Paxos Commit strengthens commit-decision fault tolerance for actual participants.
Consensus/replicated coordination cannot make arbitrary external APIs transactional participants.
Saga is independently committed subtransactions plus compensation policy, not one long ACID transaction.
Compensation is a new effect that may be imperfect, non-invertible or fail.
Orchestration is the truthful default for independent open-world systems lacking a shared commit protocol.
Transactional-outbox thinking atomically binds local state and durable intent but not later external delivery.
commitState remains scoped to Runtime operation commitment rather than external Effect commitment.
Terminal commit and admin repair batch are true Registry-local transactions without external-world rollback semantics.
Workspace mutation atomicity and replay/idempotency are separate properties.
Workspace Patch is a structured correlated multi-file effect whose mixed physical state can remain unknown rather than being misrepresented as an atomic filesystem transaction.
Atomic primitives do not automatically compose into an atomic compound operation.
Runtime Release not_committed and rolled_back are distinct histories and domain rollback does not erase Operation history.
Dual-write examples such as exchange order plus local ledger show ordering/idempotency/reconciliation improve safety without literal cross-owner ACID.
Shared Job ID, clientRequestId or coordinator state provides correlation/identity rather than atomic grouping.
Host/domain remains the current semantic multi-Operation composition owner while Runtime exposes mechanical execution/effect evidence.
The governing law is AtomicityScope <= TransactionParticipantScope.

nextRound.title: Isolation, Containment and Trust
nextRound.entryQuestion: Which execution-world components are truly isolated from one another, which are merely authority-reduced or trusted, and what non-interference guarantees can Runtime truthfully claim across process, filesystem, network, namespace, credentials and kernel boundaries?

notes: RF12 explains current local transaction and cross-owner composition boundaries but does not authorize distributed transactions, multi-Job transaction groups, a generic Saga/outbox engine, automatic compensation or production API changes.
